text_blocks.snippet: The DSM-5 (Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders, 5th Edition) outlines 11 criteria for substance use disorders, which encompass addiction. These criteria are grouped into four main categories: impaired control, physical dependence, social problems, and risky use. A diagnosis is made when two or more of these criteria are met within a 12-month period. Severity is classified as mild (2-3 symptoms), moderate (4-5), or severe (6 or more).
Here's a breakdown of the 11 criteria:

list.title: 1. Taking the substance in larger amounts or for longer than intended:
list.snippet: Individuals may use more of the substance than they planned or use it for a longer duration than desired.

list.title: 2. Persistent desire or unsuccessful efforts to cut down or control substance use:
list.snippet: There is a persistent desire to reduce or stop using the substance, but efforts to do so are unsuccessful.

list.title: 3. A great deal of time is spent in activities necessary to obtain the substance, use the substance, or recover from its effects:
list.snippet: A significant amount of time is dedicated to obtaining, using, or recovering from the effects of the substance.

list.title: 4. Craving, or a strong desire or urge to use the substance:
list.snippet: There is a strong, persistent urge or craving to use the substance.

list.title: 1. Tolerance:
list.snippet: This can be indicated by either needing markedly increased amounts of the substance to achieve the desired effect, or experiencing a markedly diminished effect with continued use of the same amount.

list.title: 2. Withdrawal:
list.snippet: This involves experiencing characteristic withdrawal symptoms when the substance is discontinued, or using the substance to relieve or avoid withdrawal symptoms.
Recurrent substance use resulting in failure to fulfill major role obligations: Substance use interferes with responsibilities at work, school, or home.
Continued substance use despite persistent or recurrent social or interpersonal problems: Substance use continues despite causing or exacerbating social or interpersonal problems.
Important social, occupational, or recreational activities are given up or reduced: Activities that were once important are given up or reduced due to substance use.

list.title: 1. Recurrent substance use in situations in which it is physically hazardous:
list.snippet: Substance use occurs in situations where it is dangerous, such as driving under the influence.

list.title: 2. Continued substance use despite knowledge of having a persistent or recurrent physical or psychological problem:
list.snippet: Substance use continues despite the individual knowing it is causing or worsening a physical or psychological problem.
